comment_data.body:
Had a quick look and, **TL;DR:**, this isn't fixable whithin `neovim`. The bug is in the `tree-sitter-idris` grammar: the bundled `array.h` breaks C strict-aliasing rules, so `gcc -O2` builds write to a `NULL` pointer. I reproduced the same 1:1 crash locally and confirmed the fix.

**Root cause**
- The grammar ships an old copy of tree-sitter's `src/tree_sitter/array.h`. Its `array_push` casts the array to `(Array *)self`, which is undefined behavior under strict aliasing.
- gcc -O2 takes advantage of that. In `push_indent`, it keeps the old `contents` pointer (NULL on the first push), calls `malloc`, stores the new pointer, then writes the element through the old NULL one. That's the segfault.
- clang doesn't compile it that way, so macOS users don't see it. Both reports are Linux builds (nix's `buildGrammar` and `:TSInstall` on Arch).

**Evidence** (same grammar revision as nix, `9fe334f`, against libtree-sitter 0.26.11, input `id' x = x`):

| Scanner build                                       | Result                  |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| clang -O2                                           | ok                      |
| gcc-16 -O2                                          | **segfault (exit 139)** |
| gcc-16 -O2 `-fno-strict-aliasing`                   | ok                      |
| gcc-16 -O2 with the `array.h` from tree-sitter 0.26 | ok                      |

Tree-sitter itself fixed this header in [tree-sitter#5242](https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter/pull/5242) and [#5194](https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter/pull/5194) (Jan 2026), but the grammar hasn't picked up the new copy yet 🤷.

This is already reported for the TS grammar as [kayhide/tree-sitter-idris#7](https://github.com/kayhide/tree-sitter-idris/issues/7) (same backtrace, crashes even on an empty file), still open with no cause found yet. The fix is to replace `src/tree_sitter/array.h` with the current template (`tree-sitter generate` with CLI ≥ 0.26 does this).
Workaround: install the idris parser from grammar (if your installation method supports it).
